issues.legal_issue: Property included within the inventory of a ruler’s private palace and lying within its mapped boundaries is excluded from the statutory definition of land and cannot vest as an estate under the land-acquisition legislation.
material_facts: The disputed parcels lay within the boundary shown on the site plan attached to the inventory of the ruler’s private property, which had been approved by the Central Government.
The State had admitted in the proceedings that the site plan was genuine and that the disputed parcels lay within the mapped boundary.
The parcels had been acquired from the former ruler, and the State had issued notices seeking possession under the land-acquisition legislation.
issues.conclusion: The parcels were excluded from the statutory definition of land, did not constitute an estate capable of vesting in the State, and could not be acquired under the Act; the notices and actions taken against the purchasers were quashed. Whether the parcels were agricultural land was immaterial to this conclusion.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 2(f), 2(b), 2(d) and 7 of the Rajasthan Land Reforms and Acquisition of Land Owners’ Estate Act, 1963, land excluded by Section 2(f)—including specified palace property in an inventory of a ruler’s private property prepared under Article 12 of the Covenant and approved by the Central Government—cannot constitute an estate under Section 2(b) or vest under Section 7. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.challenge_to_land_acquisition: A person challenged the State’s attempt to acquire land under legislation providing for acquisition of landowners’ estates.
predicates.private_property_inventory_approved: The ruler’s private-property inventory was prepared under the governing covenant and approved by the central government.
predicates.disputed_land_within_mapped_palace_bound: The disputed land lay within the boundary of palace property shown on the site plan attached to that inventory.

issues.definition: When a land-acquisition challenge concerns land within the mapped boundary of palace property in an approved private-property inventory, the land is not acquirable under the land-acquisition law.

issues.legal_issue: A transfer made after the specified date but before the commencement of a later law expressly invalidating certain transfers is not void merely because of the earlier transfer-restriction law, which treated the transferor as continuing to own the property for ceiling purposes.
material_facts: The disputed transfers were made after 16 August 1971 but before the Rajasthan Urban Property Ceiling Act, 1972 came into force.
The earlier transfer-restriction legislation provided that, despite a transfer, the property would be deemed to remain owned by the transferor; it did not declare the transfer void.
The earlier legislation was repealed in 1978.
The later ceiling legislation expressly made transfers after its commencement null and void.
issues.conclusion: The disputed transfers were not void under the earlier transfer-restriction legislation.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3(2) of the Rajasthan Urban Property (Restrictions of Transfers) Act, 1973 deemed the transferor to remain the owner for purposes of preventing evasion of the contemplated ceiling law; it did not invalidate the transfer. The 1973 Act was repealed by the Rajasthan Urban Property (Restrictions of Transfers) Repeal Act, 1978. Section 5 of the Rajasthan Urban Property Ceiling Act, 1972 invalidated transfers made after that Act commenced, but the transfers at issue preceded its commencement. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: challenge_to_transfer_validity and transfer_after_restriction_cutoff and transfer_before_absolute_transfer_ban and restriction_law_repealed

predicates.challenge_to_transfer_validity: A party challenged the validity of a transfer of urban property.
predicates.transfer_after_restriction_cutoff: The property was transferred after the date from which an earlier law applied a special ownership rule to transfers.
predicates.transfer_before_absolute_transfer_ban: The property was transferred before a later law began expressly invalidating transfers made after its commencement.
predicates.restriction_law_repealed: The earlier law imposing the special ownership rule was later repealed.

issues.definition: When a challenged transfer occurred after the earlier restriction’s cutoff but before the later absolute transfer ban, and the earlier restriction was repealed, the transfer is not void under that earlier restriction.
